notes: What the app's Dart side and its Kotlin side hand each other over the platform channel (app/lib/data/platform.dart, app/android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/eschgi/share/platform/PlatformChannel.kt). Both sides' tests read this file. server_config is what server.save stores and the downloads read; files is the argument of transfer.download (and of file.share, file.open, file.play and the keys calls): each file with its folder and, for an encrypted one (docs/e2ee-plan.md), its enc as the API gives it plus plain_size, the file's size, which Kotlin decrypts it with; the events arrive on com.eschgi.share/events. device_id is the phone's id on the server, for the proof it asks of a server over plain http (api/home_proof.json); public_verified says whether a public address over plain http passed that on this network. The upload event is the batch in upload_rows, with a few of its files: the last one sent, the one on its way and the next ones. Signed in, files go into a folder: upload.pick {what, auth, folder} and shared.send {auth, folder} name it, and the upload event says it (null with a PIN, which sends into its own). A batch whose folder is gone, or no longer the person's, is paused with folder_gone; upload.resume {auth, folder} sends it into the folder chosen instead. transfer.download, file.share, file.open and file.play take auth too: device (the default) with the phone's key over the route it picked, or pin for a PIN that shows its folder, with the PIN's key over the public address only; a PIN that ended fails only its own downloads. The transfer event is the batch in batch_items: skipped files don't count towards the totals. file.play {file} answers where the player plays a video or sound from: play_copy, a copy on the phone (saved, or fetched into the cache first over the https port at home, whose own certificate the player can't pin), or play_stream, the server with the phone's key, or with the files in a bucket play_s3, the file's link there exactly as the server signed it (a query with escapes that must stay as they are) and no key; null if the fetch was cancelled. screen.awake {on} keeps the screen on while something plays. The keys for encrypted folders live in Kotlin (keys.sync, keys.thumb, keys.decrypt and the rest of keys.*); keys.sync {password, quiet} opens them, with the password just typed, or quietly for a check-in, which neither passes through loading nor changes the status when it fails; a keys event (keys_event) says where the phone stands: status off, loading, ready, waiting or failed; has_recovery; encrypted_folders, how many the person sees; open, the folder key versions open here as folder:version; asks, whom the phone would pass keys on to after a check (docs/e2ee-plan.md): a device of the person (kind device, its name, client app or web, since when it is signed in) or a person (kind person, name, the folders they wait for, key_changed when their key was checked here before and is new now), with code once the other side answered, null before; codes, the codes this phone shows for checks others ask (kind, from: the asking device's name, code); waits_for_folders, the person waits for keys of folders they see; pace, milliseconds until the next check-in. The library lists the asks; nothing opens by itself: keys.show {kind, id} opens one (Show), which starts its check, keys.hide {kind, id} closes it (Not now) and ends the check, keys.allow {kind, id} passes the keys on after the person compared the code, keys.deny {kind, id} signs a device out (Not me); each answers the state. A keys call fails with sealed while a key isn't open here, offline without an answer, or the server's error code.
